Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cooperative commercial model for S3/pgvector adaptor and reseller split

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for taking the intro call yesterday. As discussed, Catalyst DataWorks (we're a consulting/implementation partner that builds hybrid embeddings stacks for regulated customers) is keen to accelerate a joint go-to-market with Redwood around a lightweight adapter that routes embeddings to pgvector where customers want on-prem, and S3 cold-tier for large corpora.

We sketched a commercial approach internally and attached a short term sheet. High level asks:
- Revenue split for implementation + annual support (Catalyst asks 60/40 implementation split for Year 1)
- Clarity on when Redwood will accept a bundled reseller flow vs referral fee for a self-managed deployment
- Co-branded case study rights and a 90-day pilot discount on Dedicated capacity for the proof-of-concept

Could you loop in the right Redwood folks for technical compatibility (pgvector connector semantics, S3 index fallthrough) and legal/commercial? Also copying EchoVector & Pinecone to surface any potential conflicts with existing partner programs.

We can be flexible on exact split if there's a clear path to a multi-account proof with a bank-grade customer. Proposed next step: 30-minute commercial sync early tomorrow (Friday) or Monday.

Thanks,
Marina Lopez
Head of Strategic Partnerships | Catalyst DataWorks
Mobile: +1-415-555-0182

Attachment: Catalyst_Redwood_TermSheet_v1.pdf (1 page)

Subject: Re: Cooperative commercial model for S3/pgvector adaptor and reseller split

Marina — great to get this. I reviewed the term sheet quickly; good starting point.

Quick notes from Redwood side:
- Implementation split: we typically do 50/50 for services we co-deliver if Redwood provides Dedicated credits for the POC. We can be more aggressive (60/40) if Catalyst brings the majority of pipeline and signs an annual support commitment.
- Reseller vs referral: Redwood has a reseller playbook but the partner onboarding timeline is 6–8 weeks (security paperwork + SSO + margin card). For speed, a referral + lead credit works for the first two deals.
- Technical: Ben, can you confirm compatibility constraints on pgvector + S3 fallthrough? Laura can you scope the minimum SOW for a 30-day pilot?

I'll set a 30-minute sync for tomorrow 9:30am PT unless folks request otherwise.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cooperative commercial model for S3/pgvector adaptor and reseller split

Avery / Marina — following up on compatibility. Short version: we can support a routing adapter that writes dense vectors to pgvector for low-latency lookups and falls back to S3-backed dense-index paging for archive queries. Important constraints and workitems: 

1) pgvector on customer-managed Postgres: we need a connection pattern that supports connection pooling and key rotation for high-concurrency inference; Catalyst will need to bundle a small reconnect helper (stateless) with the adapter.
2) S3 cold-tier: Redwood can host a standardized S3 index layout (Parquet + manifest) for fallthrough, but we must agree on TTL semantics and shard compaction frequency — otherwise tokenization/embedding drift will blow storage costs.
3) EchoVector / Pinecone: If your product roadmap includes a managed vector store we should explicitly map out where the adapter will prefer vendor-managed store vs pgvector or S3. Avoid overlapping reseller commitments.

I'll attach a lightweight SOW skeleton after this thread (see SOW_echo-adaptor_draft.docx). For the pilot we estimate 2 weeks engineering + 1 week integration + runway for configs in Redwood Console (routing policy + cache sizing).

Ben Carter
Director, Integrations — Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_echo-adaptor_draft.docx (editable draft)

From: Marina Lopez <partnership@catalystdw.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, EchoVector Partnerships <partners@echovector.ai>, Pinecone Sales <pinecone-sales@pinecone.io>

Subject: Re: Cooperative commercial model for S3/pgvector adaptor and reseller split

Thanks Ben — that's helpful and exactly the level we need to scope. A few clarifying points from Catalyst: 
- For pgvector we can provide a managed connection helper as an OSS crate and include it in the SOW; that resolves pooling and rotation.
- TTL/compaction: propose a default 90-day tiering policy for POC customers and a configurable compaction cron for production. We can cover compaction engineering in the implementation fee.
- For commercial overlap: EchoVector — we don't intend to displace your managed product; our focus is customers who require Postgres residency or lower infra overhead. We view EchoVector as a potential optional backend and would like to offer it in the UI as a toggle.

We can take a 50/50 implementation split if Redwood provides Dedicated credits for the pilot (covers infra for the two-week engineering sprint). If the pilot converts to paid within 90 days, Catalyst requests a carve for the first-year support margin (we proposed 10% of Redwood-recognized revenue in the term sheet).

On the sync: 9:30am PT tomorrow works for me. See you then.

Hi all — quick note from EchoVector. Appreciate the heads-up. We like the idea of being an optional backend toggle in the adapter UI. Two asks from EchoVector:
1) Please include a short clause in the partner term sheet that any customer-facing technical collateral referencing EchoVector is reviewed by our partnerships team before publication.
2) For go-to-market simplicity, EchoVector would prefer referrals in the first 6 months of any joint POC (no straight reseller commitments) — after that we can re-evaluate margining once we see conversion velocity.

Ben — we're happy to jump on the sync or provide a short technical note on our connector compatibility and capacity guidance.

Best,
Ishan Rao
